name: Light teal tone
lede: Light teal tone translates Asagi-iro (浅葱色), a traditional Japanese blue-green named for the pale color of a scallion shoot.

sections.title: A scallion-shoot blue-green
sections.body:
Our color graph files this hue as a Japanese traditional color, *Asagi-iro* (浅葱色), whose kanji combine "pale" and "scallion" and whose standard meaning is given simply as "light blue color" [1]. It carries no separate Ridgway or ISCC-NBS record in our sources, unlike most of its western-numbered neighbors [1]. English-language use files it here as "Light teal tone," with [[teal]] itself as a wider, better-known sibling name for this family of dark blue-greens [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[capri-blue|Capri Blue]], 4.9 units away and darker, with [[cadet-blue|Cadet Blue]] close behind at 5.1, greener and lighter [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this blue-green in 57 of 23,781 paintings (0.24 percent, as photographed), rarer than 59 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It most often plays a light, in 46 percent of its strongest matches, and peaks in paintings from the 1900s at 2.2 times the expected rate [2]. The earliest dated match runs to 1445, by Domenico Veneziano; a floor, not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin and our sources carry no fixed-record date for this name to compare it against [2].
